newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-GANGULY LEADS WAY FOR INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GANGULY LEADS WAY FOR INDIA.

text.p: A one-day international career best of 83 by opener Saurav Ganguly anchored India to 233 for five in their triangular tournament match against South Africa on Tuesday.
The left-hander easily passed his previous best of 59, made against Australia, before becoming the second run out victim of the innings when he and Ajay Jadeja ended up at the same end.
Ganguly pulled Jacques Kallis for six early in his innings and hit six fours in a 136-ball stay to register India's highest individual score in their four matches so far in the tournament.
He shared a 117-run opening partnership with Rahul Dravid (53) but India failed to capitalise on the good start on the compact, high scoring Buffalo Park ground.
Sachin Tendulkar (14) and Mohammad Azharuddin (13) fell cheaply when India needed to accelerate and it was left to all-rounder Robin Singh with 32 in just 21 balls to lift the innings.
After two defeats by South Africa and a tie with Zimbabwe, India desperately need a win to boost their chances of qualifying for the final in Durban on February 12.
